questions.key_step: Double-count incidences for both families and equate the two values of |T|.
questions.justification: One familiar double-counting identity applied twice; no decision or casework (like 2021-P2-Q17, L1).

questions.key_step: Cancel (x-2) to get g, then solve -1 <= g <= 1 as two rational inequalities and intersect.
questions.justification: Standard domain-of-composite chain: limit to define g(2), two sign-scheme inequalities, intersection. Routine multi-step with no real insight (L2).

questions.key_step: Bound each [kr] by kr-1 < [kr] <= kr, sum, divide by n^2 and sandwich.
questions.justification: Single standard sandwich with the greatest-integer inequality and an AP sum; a few routine steps (L2).

questions.key_step: Let the common ratio be K; a+b = (pi/2)/K and c = tan^{-1}y / K, so pi c/(a+b) = 2 tan^{-1} y.
questions.justification: Single standard identity (sin^-1 x + cos^-1 x = pi/2) with a ratio substitution, then cos 2θ formula; three routine steps (L2).

questions.key_step: Conditions decouple into a1|b2 and a2|b1, each counted by the same 6 pairs; answer 6x6.
questions.justification: Short enumeration of divisor pairs and a product; the decoupling is the only observation needed (like a counting relation, no equivalence, L2).

questions.key_step: Find explicit counterexamples: (2,1) in R but (1,2) not; (1,3),(3,2) in R but (1,2) not.
questions.justification: Three property checks, each settled by a small counterexample; the options require checking symmetry and transitivity, not just reflexivity.

questions.key_step: Apply the equation at x = 2, -1, 1/2 (the 3-cycle) and combine to isolate f(2).
questions.justification: One recognised cycle trick then a 3-equation linear solve; short but chained (L2).

questions.key_step: Solve the recurrence f(n)=n f(1), then test each statement (injectivity transfer for composites, surjective f forces f(1)=1).
questions.justification: Four statements each needing a genuine check, with a recurrence solve and composition theorems; no heavy computation (L3).

questions.key_step: Compute f(g(n)) = ceil(n/2) piecewise; it takes every natural value, each twice.
questions.justification: Compute a composite of two piecewise functions and test injectivity and surjectivity; a few routine steps (L2).

questions.key_step: Range of f = {2,4,6,8,10}; g(f(k))=f(k) forces g(y)=y on the range, leaving 10 free choices for each of the 5 odd inputs.
questions.justification: One structural observation (g is pinned only on Range f) then a power count; short, no casework (L3 in an Advanced context because the idea is slightly unfamiliar).

questions.key_step: Rewrite the term as tan^{-1}((3/2)^{r+1}) - tan^{-1}((3/2)^r) and telescope.
questions.justification: Same telescoping-difference idea as 2021-P1-Q15 (L4) but with the pattern clearly signalled by 1+ab in the denominator; routine chain (L2).

questions.key_step: LHL = 1/|λ-1| and RHL = 1/|λ|; equate to get λ=1/2, L=2.
questions.justification: Two one-sided limits and one absolute-value equation; routine multi-step with no insight (L2).

questions.key_step: Sum of 2p gives 1+n(n+1); then cot^{-1}(1+n(n+1)) = tan^{-1}(n+1)-tan^{-1}n.
questions.justification: Standard telescoping pattern with 1+n(n+1); a few routine steps (L2); easier than 2021-P1-Q15.

questions.key_step: Use the root condition to make the cos argument (x-2p)^2, evaluate the limit 1/2, and determine that f stays just below 1/2.
questions.justification: Root condition, a 1-cos u over u^2 standard limit, and a one-sided floor argument; the 'approach from below' check is where students slip (L3).

questions.key_step: Find where |x| = x^2 (x = 0, ±1, with different slopes there) and check the junctions x = ±2.
questions.justification: Graph-based search for corners of a max function plus junction checks; missing any one of five points gives a wrong option, but options help (L3).

questions.key_step: Triples sum to 3(r-1), numerator = 3n(n-1)/2; multiply by the conjugate in the denominator and compare leading terms.
questions.justification: Grouping, an AP sum and a conjugate rationalisation; routine chain of three standard steps (L2).

questions.key_step: Factor out n^{cosec^2 t}; the remaining bracket tends to 1 because every (k/n)^{m} with k<n tends to 0.
questions.justification: One familiar trick (the largest term dominates); applied once (L1).

questions.key_step: Read alpha=2, beta=-1 from the graphs, so x -> -alpha*beta = 2; cancel (x-2) and substitute.
questions.justification: Two direct vertex readings and one 0/0 cancellation; a single routine idea, applied once (L1).

questions.key_step: Note (5+2sqrt6)+(5-2sqrt6)=10 with product 1, so exponent (x^2-4)/2 must be +1 or -1.
questions.justification: Spot that the bases are reciprocal and sum to 10 after squaring, then solve two quadratics; two linked ideas with simple execution (L2).
Standard solve of the exponential functional equation then a GP sum (L2).
